title: Resolve a user principal from a verified Cognito token
description:
**Phase 3 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 1ebc7d, 0df6cb, 272aea
- **Runs in parallel with:** fac2ee, 5558db, 41d08d, and 79578e
- **Unblocks:** 22f5bb, 7b4616

---
Verify the bearer token against the Cognito JWKS, map the verified email to an Identity, load Membership, and build the Principal. Cache the JWKS and the membership read for the warm life of the function; the front door already reads DynamoDB per request, so one more GetItem costs nothing at this scale and buys real revocation.

Nothing about organizations, roles, or ceilings travels in the token. The token says who you are; standing is resolved server side, per request.

**Done when:** behave and pytest cover a valid token, an expired token, an unknown email, and a suspended organization, and routes still do not enforce.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Adversarial review: a turn stream outlives the check.**

A turn-scoped SSE stream is held for up to 900 seconds, and the measurements in docs/DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md show reconnects with Last-Event-ID. The token is validated when the stream opens. Decide now whether it is validated again during the stream.

If it is validated once, a member whose membership is revoked mid-turn keeps receiving output for the rest of that turn. That may be perfectly acceptable at this scale, but it should be a recorded decision rather than something discovered later during an incident.

Also confirm the reconnect path carries a fresh token. A client that reconnects after fifteen minutes with the original token will fail in a way that looks like a stream bug.
